literature.headline_zh: 汉坦病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期汉坦病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 研究发现,ANDV是一种人畜共患的正汉坦病毒,在智利南部和阿根廷流行,主要病毒为Oligoryzomys longicaudatus 储存宿主。报告还报道,美洲每年大约发生 300 例汉坦病毒心肺综合征病例。 [10.1111/eci.70255]

共识别出215例汉坦病毒肺综合征(HCPS)患者,其中69.3%为男性,87%为成人。在148例需要呼吸支持的患者中,14.2%接受了无创通气(NIV),36.5%接受了机械通气(MV),49.3%需要体外膜氧合(ECMO)。住院时间中位数为8天[3-15],住院期间死亡率为20.5%。接受机械通气患者的病死率为29.6%,接受ECMO患者的病死率为32.9%。大流行期间与更高的住院期间死亡率独立相关(校正优势比2.73 [1.06-7.63];p = 0.045)。 [10.1007/s00134-026-08599-9]
斯洛文尼亚和克罗地亚在东南欧地区表现出最高的 HFRS 累积负担,2008 年、2012 年、2014 年、2017 年、2019 年、2021 年和 2023 年多个邻国的活动部分同步增加。这些模式与共同的生态影响相一致,包括啮齿动物种群波动、肥大播种事件和气候变化。 [10.17305/bb.2026.14790]
内皮功能障碍是严重汉坦病毒疾病的病理标志,由 VEGF 敏化、Src 激酶和 RhoA 通路激活、周细胞感染以及包括 IL-6 反式信号传导在内的炎症反应失调驱动。诊断策略依赖于 血清学 和分子检测,而管理仍然主要是支持性的,体外膜肺氧合 (ECMO) 可以提高暴发性 HCPS 的生存率。 [10.1002/rmv.70191]

key_findings_en: The study found that ANDV is a zoonotic orthohantavirus endemic in southern Chile and Argentina, with Oligoryzomys longicaudatus as its principal reservoir. It also reported that approximately 300 cases of hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome occur annually in the Americas. [10.1111/eci.70255]

A total of 215 patients with HCPS were identified, of whom 69.3% were males and 87% were adults. Of 148 patients who required respiratory support, 14.2% received NIV, 36.5% received MV and 49.3% required ECMO. Hospital LOS was 8 [3-15] days and in-hospital mortality was 20.5%. [10.1007/s00134-026-08599-9]

Slovenia and Croatia exhibit the highest cumulative burden of HFRS in SEE, with partially synchronized increases in activity across multiple neighboring countries in 2008, 2012, 2014, 2017, 2019, 2021, and 2023. [10.17305/bb.2026.14790]
Hantavirus infections have been reported primarily in Europe, Asia, and. [10.1080/23744235.2026.2724015]

Endothelial dysfunction is the pathological hallmark of severe hantavirus disease, driven by VEGF sensitisation, Src kinase and RhoA pathway activation, pericyte infection, and dysregulated inflammatory responses including IL-6 trans-signalling. [10.1002/rmv.70191]

papers.title: Hantavirus infections in Southeastern Europe – Epidemiology, outbreak dynamics, and One Health preparedness: A narrative review
papers.abstract: Human-pathogenic orthohantaviruses are significant rodent-borne zoonotic pathogens in Europe. Southeastern Europe (SEE) is a distinct endemic region where Dobrava-Belgrade virus (DOBV) and Puumala virus (PUUV) co-circulate, causing hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) of varying severity. This narrative review synthesizes the epidemiology, transmission dynamics, clinical characteristics, ecological drivers, and public health challenges of hantavirus infections across SEE, identifying priorities for regional preparedness. We searched PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science from their inception through June 2026, supplementing with reference screening. Regional epidemiological patterns were assessed descriptively using national surveillance data, European surveillance reports, published studies, and available population-based incidence estimates. Long-term surveillance reveals persistent endemic transmission with significant geographic and interannual heterogeneity. Slovenia and Croatia exhibit the highest cumulative burden and most pronounced periods of increased HFRS activity. Several years—2008, 2012, 2014, 2017, 2019, 2021, and 2023—showed partially synchronized increases across multiple neighboring countries. These patterns align with shared ecological influences, including rodent population fluctuations, mast-seeding events, and climatic variability. However, local ecology, human exposure, and differences in surveillance capacity modify their magnitude. The coexistence of generally milder PUUV-associated disease and more severe DOBV-associated HFRS further distinguishes SEE's clinical landscape. Therefore, hantavirus epidemiology in SEE is best understood as an interconnected regional ecological system. Integrated human, animal, environmental, and genomic surveillance within a coordinated One Health framework is crucial for improving outbreak prediction, cross-border preparedness, and future disease control.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述检查了东南欧 (SEE) 的人类致病性正汉坦病毒,重点关注多布拉瓦-贝尔格莱德病毒 (DOBV) 和普马拉病毒 (PUUV),作为导致该地区不同严重程度的 肾综合征出血热 (HFRS) 的主要目标实体。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 这篇叙述性综述检索了 PubMed、Scopus 和 Web of Science 从成立到 2026 年 6 月的数据,并补充了参考文献筛选。使用国家 监测 数据、欧洲 监测 报告、已发表的研究和基于人群的 发病率 估计值对区域流行病学模式进行描述性评估。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 斯洛文尼亚和克罗地亚在东南欧地区表现出最高的 HFRS 累积负担,2008 年、2012 年、2014 年、2017 年、2019 年、2021 年和 2023 年多个邻国的活动部分同步增加。这些模式与共同的生态影响相一致,包括啮齿动物种群波动、肥大播种事件和气候变化。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述强调了持续流行的 传播 在 SEE 中具有显着的地理和年际异质性,表明当地生态、人类暴露和 监测 容量的未解决的变异性改变了 暴发 的强度。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 在一个协调的“同一个健康”框架内整合人类、动物、环境和 基因组监测 对于改善 SEE 的 暴发 预测、跨境准备和未来疾病控制至关重要。

papers.title_zh: 东南欧的汉坦病毒感染 – 流行病学、暴发 动态和 One Health 准备:叙述性回顾
papers.source_body_en: Human-pathogenic orthohantaviruses are significant rodent-borne zoonotic pathogens in Europe. Southeastern Europe (SEE) is a distinct endemic region where Dobrava-Belgrade virus (DOBV) and Puumala virus (PUUV) co-circulate, causing hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) of varying severity. This narrative review synthesizes the epidemiology, transmission dynamics, clinical characteristics, ecological drivers, and public health challenges of hantavirus infections across SEE, identifying priorities for regional preparedness. We searched PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science from their inception through June 2026, supplementing with reference screening. Regional epidemiological patterns were assessed descriptively using national surveillance data, European surveillance reports, published studies, and available population-based incidence estimates. Long-term surveillance reveals persistent endemic transmission with significant geographic and interannual heterogeneity. Slovenia and Croatia exhibit the highest cumulative burden and most pronounced periods of increased HFRS activity. Several years—2008, 2012, 2014, 2017, 2019, 2021, and 2023—showed partially synchronized increases across multiple neighboring countries. These patterns align with shared ecological influences, including rodent population fluctuations, mast-seeding events, and climatic variability. However, local ecology, human exposure, and differences in surveillance capacity modify their magnitude. The coexistence of generally milder PUUV-associated disease and more severe DOBV-associated HFRS further distinguishes SEE's clinical landscape. Therefore, hantavirus epidemiology in SEE is best understood as an interconnected regional ecological system. Integrated human, animal, environmental, and genomic surveillance within a coordinated One Health framework is crucial for improving outbreak prediction, cross-border preparedness, and future disease control.

papers.title: Andes Virus: From Transmission Dynamics to Pandemic Potential
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Andes virus (ANDV) has recently emerged as a significant public health concern following a multi‐country outbreak aboard the MV Hondius cruise ship in April 2026, with 13 identified cases and three deaths among passengers and crew. Methods We reviewed available literature from PubMed and Google Scholar databases and searched international health agencies, including the World Health Organisation and national public health authorities, for current outbreak information and up‐to‐date epidemiological data. Results ANDV is a zoonotic orthohantavirus endemic in southern Chile and Argentina, with Oligoryzomys longicaudatus as its principal reservoir. Approximately 300 cases of hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome occur annually in the Americas. The virus causes severe disease through endothelial dysfunction and vascular leakage, resulting in rapidly progressive pulmonary edema and shock. Human‐to‐human transmission is characteristic of ANDV and occurs through respiratory and salivary routes during prolonged close contact. Clinical presentation includes nonspecific prodromal symptoms followed by rapid cardiopulmonary deterioration. Diagnosis relies on serological assays and RT‐qPCR. Management is predominantly supportive, emphasising hemodynamic monitoring and early consideration of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation in severe cases. Conclusions Despite ANDV's severity and high mortality, its epidemic potential seems to be low. However, the recent outbreak underscores the importance of international surveillance coordination and rapid diagnostic capabilities for emerging zoonotic infections.

papers.title: The Changing Landscape of Hantavirus Infections: A Narrative Review of Epidemiology, Pathogenesis, and Countermeasures.
papers.abstract: Hantaviruses are emerging zoonotic pathogens of increasing global public health significance. Their epidemiological landscape is rapidly changing due to ecological disruption, climate variability, urbanisation, and evolving human-animal interfaces. This narrative review synthesises current knowledge on hantavirus virology, epidemiology, pathogenesis, clinical management, and emerging countermeasures, with a focus on developments from the past 5 years. Traditionally classified into Old World viruses causing haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and New World viruses causing hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS), this dichotomy has become increasingly blurred, with overlapping renal and pulmonary manifestations now recognized. Among the most consequential recent advances is the consolidated evidence for person-to-person transmission of Andes virus, documented among household contacts and during the prodromal phase, with viral shedding in respiratory secretions. Endothelial dysfunction remains the pathological hallmark of severe disease, driven by VEGF sensitisation, Src kinase and RhoA pathway activation, pericyte infection, and dysregulated inflammatory responses including IL-6 trans-signalling. Concurrently, environmental and ecological studies have linked climate change, rodent population dynamics, land-use modification, and urbanisation to increased human disease risk across multiple continents. Diagnostic strategies continue to rely on serology and molecular testing, while management remains predominantly supportive, with extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) improving survival in fulminant HCPS. Importantly, recent structural virology advances have enabled the development of broadly neutralising monoclonal antibodies targeting conserved quaternary epitopes, as well as next-generation vaccine platforms including DNA, mRNA, and prefusion-stabilised glycoprotein candidates. Hantaviruses represent a paradigmatic One Health challenge at the intersection of environmental change, viral evolution, and global interconnectedness. Despite major progress in understanding transmission dynamics and endothelial pathogenesis, critical gaps remain regarding determinants of person-to-person spread, long-term post-infection sequelae, and the absence of licenced broadly protective vaccines or specific antiviral therapies. Future preparedness will require integrated surveillance frameworks combining ecological monitoring, genomic epidemiology, and clinical readiness within coordinated international public health strategies.

papers.title_zh: 汉坦病毒 感染的变化格局:流行病学、发病机制 和对策的叙述回顾。
papers.source_body_en: Hantaviruses are emerging zoonotic pathogens of increasing global public health significance. Their epidemiological landscape is rapidly changing due to ecological disruption, climate variability, urbanisation, and evolving human-animal interfaces. This narrative review synthesises current knowledge on hantavirus virology, epidemiology, pathogenesis, clinical management, and emerging countermeasures, with a focus on developments from the past 5 years. Traditionally classified into Old World viruses causing haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and New World viruses causing hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS), this dichotomy has become increasingly blurred, with overlapping renal and pulmonary manifestations now recognized. Among the most consequential recent advances is the consolidated evidence for person-to-person transmission of Andes virus, documented among household contacts and during the prodromal phase, with viral shedding in respiratory secretions. Endothelial dysfunction remains the pathological hallmark of severe disease, driven by VEGF sensitisation, Src kinase and RhoA pathway activation, pericyte infection, and dysregulated inflammatory responses including IL-6 trans-signalling. Concurrently, environmental and ecological studies have linked climate change, rodent population dynamics, land-use modification, and urbanisation to increased human disease risk across multiple continents. Diagnostic strategies continue to rely on serology and molecular testing, while management remains predominantly supportive, with extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) improving survival in fulminant HCPS. Importantly, recent structural virology advances have enabled the development of broadly neutralising monoclonal antibodies targeting conserved quaternary epitopes, as well as next-generation vaccine platforms including DNA, mRNA, and prefusion-stabilised glycoprotein candidates. Hantaviruses represent a paradigmatic One Health challenge at the intersection of environmental change, viral evolution, and global interconnectedness. Despite major progress in understanding transmission dynamics and endothelial pathogenesis, critical gaps remain regarding determinants of person-to-person spread, long-term post-infection sequelae, and the absence of licenced broadly protective vaccines or specific antiviral therapies. Future preparedness will require integrated surveillance frameworks combining ecological monitoring, genomic epidemiology, and clinical readiness within coordinated international public health strategies.

papers.title: Temporal trends in critical care burden and outcomes of Andes virus-associated hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome: a national Chilean cohort
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: Andes virus causes hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS), a severe disease found in central and southern parts of Chile and Argentina. Recently a case-outbreak of HCPS was reported on a cruise ship, therefore contemporary data on organ support and outcomes is required. The objective of this study was to assess organ support use and patient outcomes in patients admitted with HCPS. METHODS: We used the Diagnosis-Related Groups (DGR) database to analyse patients admitted in 31 Chilean hospitals between January 1, 2019, and December 31, 2024. They were stratified by the maximal respiratory support received: no respiratory support, non-invasive ventilation (NIV), invasive mechanical ventilation (MV) or extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). Hospital length of stay (LOS) and in-hospital mortality were the main outcomes assessed. In-hospital mortality was further analysed by pre-COVID-19 pandemic, pandemic, and post-pandemic periods. RESULTS: A total of 215 patients with HCPS were identified, of whom 69.3% were males and 87% were adults. Of 148 patients who required respiratory support, 14.2% received NIV, 36.5% received MV and 49.3% required ECMO. Hospital LOS was 8 [3-15] days and in-hospital mortality was 20.5%. Case fatality rates were 29.6% for patients receiving MV and 32.9% for those receiving ECMO. The pandemic period was independently associated with higher in-hospital mortality (aOR 2.73 [1.06-7.63]; p = 0.045). CONCLUSION: HCPS caused by Andes virus remains associated with high in-hospital mortality and substantial amounts of respiratory support, particularly MV and ECMO. Moreover, the COVID-19 pandemic was associated with a significant increase in HCPS mortality.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the temporal trends in critical care burden and outcomes of Andes virus-associated hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS) in Chile. It highlights the high in-hospital mortality and significant use of respiratory support, particularly mechanical ventilation and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, among patients with HCPS. The research also identifies a notable increase in mortality during the pandemic period, suggesting potential impacts of pandemic-related factors on HCPS outcomes. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the observational design and possible confounding variables.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究的目的是评估 HCPS 入院患者的器官支持使用情况和患者预后。我们使用 诊断 相关群体 (DGR) 数据库分析了 2019 年 1 月 1 日至 2024 年 12 月 31 日期间在 31 家智利医院收治的患者。
elements_zh.methods: They were stratified by the maximal respiratory support received: no respiratory support,non-invasive ventilation (NIV),invasive mechanical ventilation (MV) or extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO).住院时间 (LOS) 和住院 死亡率 是评估的主要结果。按 COVID-19 大流行前、大流行和大流行后时期进一步分析了院内 死亡率。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: Andes virus causes hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS), a severe disease found in central and southern parts of Chile and Argentina. Recently a case-outbreak of HCPS was reported on a cruise ship, therefore contemporary data on organ support and outcomes is required.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The objective of this study was to assess organ support use and patient outcomes in patients admitted with HCPS. We used the Diagnosis-Related Groups (DGR) database to analyse patients admitted in 31 Chilean hospitals between January 1, 2019, and December 31, 2024.
analysis_en.methods: They were stratified by the maximal respiratory support received: no respiratory support, non-invasive ventilation (NIV), invasive mechanical ventilation (MV) or extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). Hospital length of stay (LOS) and in-hospital mortality were the main outcomes assessed. In-hospital mortality was further analysed by pre-COVID-19 pandemic, pandemic, and post-pandemic periods.
analysis_en.main_results: A total of 215 patients with HCPS were identified, of whom 69.3% were males and 87% were adults. Of 148 patients who required respiratory support, 14.2% received NIV, 36.5% received MV and 49.3% required ECMO. Hospital LOS was 8 [3-15] days and in-hospital mortality was 20.5%. Case fatality rates were 29.6% for patients receiving MV and 32.9% for those receiving ECMO. The pandemic period was independently associated with higher in-hospital mortality (aOR 2.73 [1.06-7.63]; p = 0.045).
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: HCPS caused by Andes virus remains associated with high in-hospital mortality and substantial amounts of respiratory support, particularly MV and ECMO. Moreover, the COVID-19 pandemic was associated with a significant increase in HCPS mortality.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the ongoing burden of HCPS in Chile and the impact of the pandemic on its mortality rates, informing the need for improved surveillance and targeted interventions.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on a Diagnosis-Related Groups (DGR) database, which may have limitations in capturing detailed clinical information. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the observational nature of the study and potential confounding factors.

papers.title_zh: 安第斯病毒相关汉坦病毒心肺综合征的重症监护负担和结果的时间趋势:智利国家 队列研究
papers.source_body_en: PURPOSE: Andes virus causes hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS), a severe disease found in central and southern parts of Chile and Argentina. Recently a case-outbreak of HCPS was reported on a cruise ship, therefore contemporary data on organ support and outcomes is required. The objective of this study was to assess organ support use and patient outcomes in patients admitted with HCPS. METHODS: We used the Diagnosis-Related Groups (DGR) database to analyse patients admitted in 31 Chilean hospitals between January 1, 2019, and December 31, 2024. They were stratified by the maximal respiratory support received: no respiratory support, non-invasive ventilation (NIV), invasive mechanical ventilation (MV) or extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). Hospital length of stay (LOS) and in-hospital mortality were the main outcomes assessed. In-hospital mortality was further analysed by pre-COVID-19 pandemic, pandemic, and post-pandemic periods. RESULTS: A total of 215 patients with HCPS were identified, of whom 69.3% were males and 87% were adults. Of 148 patients who required respiratory support, 14.2% received NIV, 36.5% received MV and 49.3% required ECMO. Hospital LOS was 8 [3-15] days and in-hospital mortality was 20.5%. Case fatality rates were 29.6% for patients receiving MV and 32.9% for those receiving ECMO. The pandemic period was independently associated with higher in-hospital mortality (aOR 2.73 [1.06-7.63]; p = 0.045). CONCLUSION: HCPS caused by Andes virus remains associated with high in-hospital mortality and substantial amounts of respiratory support, particularly MV and ECMO. Moreover, the COVID-19 pandemic was associated with a significant increase in HCPS mortality.

papers.title: The necessity of adding Hantavirus infection to the differential diagnosis of Iran syndromic surveillance
papers.abstract: Iran’s syndromic surveillance system is continuously monitoring emerging infectious diseases. Given the serological and molecular evidence of hantavirus circulation in rodent reservoirs and the human population of the country, strengthening diagnostic approaches in this system is important. In addition to presenting with manifestations such as renal and respiratory syndromes, hantavirus requires a distinct place in the differential diagnosis protocols of acute respiratory and influenza-like infections. Utilizing existing laboratory capacities, along with ongoing training for early identification of suspicious cases, can significantly strengthen the current surveillance system in managing possible outbreaks and responding to these potential threats

papers.title: Predicting the potential distribution of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome in Southwest China using the ecological niche modeling
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) severely burdens China's public health. With its complex topography and rich biodiversity, Southwest China has historically incubated this natural focal disease. Currently, traditional environmental drivers of transmission here are increasingly eclipsed by anthropogenic forces, notably population agglomeration. Driven by these shifting dynamics, HFRS incidence and endemic ranges are expanding, yet systematic, regional-scale assessments remain scarce. Consequently, this study employs ecological niche modeling to map potential high-risk zones. Ultimately, we aim to explore the core mechanisms driving HFRS prevalence amid the complex interplay of natural environments and human activities. Methods Surveillance data of HFRS cases in Southwest China from 2014 to 2023 were obtained from the China Information System for Disease Control and Prevention (CISDCP). A Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt) model was constructed by integrating occurrence records with multisource environmental variables, including meteorological, socioeconomic, and land cover factors. Model performance was evaluated using the Area Under the Curve (AUC) of the Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC), and the Jackknife test was employed to quantify the contribution of each variable. Results The MaxEnt model demonstrated robust predictive performance with a mean AUC of 0.902. Population density was identified as the predominant predictor (73.5% contribution), followed by the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) in May (9.2%) and annual mean temperature (5.8%). The spatial distribution of risk exhibited a core aggregation with sporadic dispersion pattern, with high-risk zones concentrated in the Chengdu-Chongqing urban agglomeration and localized clusters in Yunnan Province. Response curves revealed a sigmoidal positive correlation between population density and disease risk. Meteorological factors, such as temperature and precipitation, exhibited non-linear inverted U-shaped or U-shaped relationships, constraining the spatial boundaries of transmission. Conclusions The spatial heterogeneity of HFRS in Southwest China is jointly driven by anthropogenic activities and natural environmental constraints. Human population density acts as the primary amplifier of transmission risk, supporting the human behavior amplification effect in natural focal diseases. These findings suggest a strategic shift from blanket prevention to precision control, prioritizing active surveillance in densely populated urban fringes and areas undergoing infrastructure development.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 肾综合征出血热(HFRS)严重影响了中国的公共卫生。中国西南地区地形复杂,生物多样性丰富,历史上孕育了这种自然疫源性疾病。目前,传播 的传统环境驱动因素日益被人为力量(尤其是人口集聚)所掩盖。在这些动态变化的推动下,HFRS 发病率 和流行范围正在扩大,但系统的、区域规模的评估仍然很少。因此,本研究采用生态位模型来绘制潜在的高风险区域。最终,我们的目标是在自然环境和人类活动复杂的相互作用中探索驱动 HFRS 患病率 的核心机制。方法从中国疾病预防控制信息系统(CISDCP)获取2014年至2023年中国西南地区HFRS病例监测数据。通过将事件记录与多源环境变量(包括气象、社会经济和土地覆盖因素)相结合,构建了最大熵(MaxEnt)模型。使用接受者操作特征 (ROC) 的曲线下面积 (AUC) 评估模型性能,并采用 Jackknife 测试来量化每个变量的贡献。结果 MaxEnt 模型表现出稳健的预测性能,平均 AUC 为 0.902。人口密度被确定为主要预测因素(贡献 73.5%),其次是 5 月份的归一化植被指数 (NDVI)(9.2%)和年平均气温(5.8%)。风险空间分布呈现核心聚集、零星分散的格局,高风险区集中在成渝城市群和云南省局部集群。反应曲线显示人口密度和疾病风险之间呈 S 形正相关。气温、降水等气象因素呈现非线性倒U型或U型关系,制约了传播的空间边界。结论 西南地区HFRS空间异质性是由人类活动和自然环境约束共同驱动的。人口密度是 传播 风险的主要放大器,支持自然疫源性疾病中人类行为的放大效应。这些发现表明从全面预防到精准控制的战略转变,优先在人口稠密的城市边缘和正在进行基础设施开发的地区积极开展监测。

papers.title: Delayed and Heterogeneous Effects of Flood Exposure on Hemorrhagic Fever with Renal Syndrome Risk: A Nationwide Spatiotemporal and Quasi-Experimental Study
papers.abstract: Abstract Floods are increasingly frequent under climate change and may influence zoonotic disease transmission through environmental and ecological pathways. However, the spatiotemporal heterogeneity and potential causal relationship between floods and disease risk remain insufficiently characterized. We combined nationwide surveillance data on hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) with multisource flood records in China from 2005 to 2022 to evaluate the association between flood exposure and HFRS risk. A Bayesian spatiotemporal hierarchical model was used to estimate lagged associations, identify high-risk clusters, and assess effect modification by environmental and socioeconomic factors. To strengthen causal inference, we further applied a stacked difference-in-differences design with propensity score matching. Flood exposure was associated with a biphasic lagged response in HFRS risk, characterized by a short-term decrease during the flood month and the subsequent month, followed by a delayed increase peaking at 4–6 months (maximum at 5 months: RR = 1.05, 95% CrI 1.02–1.08). Spatially, elevated risks were concentrated in flood-prone areas, particularly in northeast China. The delayed increase in risk was more pronounced in midtemperate regions, Apodemus-type endemic areas, and agricultural zones. Effect modification analyses indicated higher flood-associated risks in areas with lower socioeconomic status, including lower GDP, limited healthcare resources, and lower agricultural mechanization. The quasi-experimental analysis supported a causal association between flood exposure and increased HFRS risk, with the largest effect observed at approximately 3 months post-flood. These findings are consistent with environmentally mediated changes in host ecology and human exposure that may influence disease transmission following flood events. Our results provide evidence that flood exposure can increase zoonotic disease risk with a delayed and spatially heterogeneous pattern. Accounting for these lagged and context-specific effects may improve risk assessment and inform targeted public health interventions following extreme hydrological events.

papers.title: Burning down the mouse: Effects of wildfire and post-fire reseeding on Sin Nombre virus prevalence in its reservoir host
papers.abstract: Worldwide, physical habitats and biological communities are being reshaped by wildfire. Such changes have obvious potential to alter pathogen ecology, yet few studies, outside of those focused on ectoparasites, have tested the effects of wildfire on pathogen prevalence in wildlife. Even fewer have focused on the impacts of strategies for post-fire remediation on pathogen circulation. Here, we investigated the effect of wildfire and wildfire mitigation on the prevalence and viral load of Sin Nombre virus (SNV) infection in its reservoir host, the western deer mouse, using a study design of matched burned, unburned, and post-burn reseeded sites in northern New Mexico. In total, we screened 411 individual deer mice for SNV via RT-qPCR and analyzed the effect of wildfire and wildfire mitigation on relative mouse abundance, individual infection probability, site-level prevalence and viral load. Relative abundance was highest at reseeded sites, and model selection indicated that habitat structure, particularly the gradient from closed canopy to open-herbaceous habitat, was consistently associated with increased relative abundance. Similarly, SNV prevalence was significantly higher in reseeded sites than either burned or unburned sites but did not differ in burned versus unburned sites. Viral load did not differ between burn history types, and zero-inflated gamma hurdle models did not identify any strong predictors of viral load. Serendipitously, we were also able to investigate the impacts of an El Nino Southern Oscillation (ENSO) cycle on patterns of infection in a subsample of sites that were studied during and one year after an ENSO year and found that SNV prevalence increased significantly post-ENSO. Both reseeding and ENSO deliver resource pulses that can support increases in mouse density and thereby enhance SNV transmission. The impacts of post-fire management practices on SNV prevalence in its reservoir host that were revealed in this study should be considered when implementing such strategies and when utilizing treated areas.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究在新墨西哥州北部设计了匹配的火烧区、未火烧区和火后重播种区。研究筛查了411只单独的鹿鼠(Peromyscus maniculatus)个体的辛诺柏病毒(SNV)感染情况,并分析了野火及其缓解措施对相对鼠类丰度、感染概率、场地级患病率及病毒载量的影响。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员使用 RT-qPCR 筛选个体鹿小鼠的 SNV,并应用零膨胀伽玛障碍模型来分析野火和火灾后重新播种对相对丰度、感染概率、位点水平 患病率 和病毒载量的影响。
elements_zh.main_results: 重新播种地点的鹿鼠相对丰度最高。与烧毁或未烧毁地点相比,重新播种地点的 SNV 患病率 显着较高,但烧毁和未烧毁地点之间的 患病率 没有差异。烧伤史类型之间的病毒载量没有差异,并且没有发现病毒载量的强预测因子。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: Wildfire is reshaping habitats and biological communities globally, with potential impacts on pathogen ecology. Few studies have examined how wildfire affects pathogen prevalence in wildlife, particularly focusing on the effects of post-fire remediation strategies.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study employed a design of matched burned, unburned, and post-burn reseeded sites in northern New Mexico. It screened 411 individual deer mice for Sin Nombre virus (SNV) and analyzed the effect of wildfire and mitigation on relative mouse abundance, infection probability, site-level prevalence, and viral load.
analysis_en.methods: The researchers used RT-qPCR to screen individual deer mice for SNV and applied zero-inflated gamma hurdle models to analyze the effect of wildfire and post-fire reseeding on relative abundance, infection probability, site-level prevalence, and viral load.
analysis_en.main_results: Relative abundance of deer mice was highest at reseeded sites. SNV prevalence was significantly higher in reseeded sites compared to burned or unburned sites, but there was no difference in prevalence between burned and unburned sites. Viral load did not differ between burn history types, and no strong predictors of viral load were identified.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that post-fire reseeding may increase SNV prevalence in its reservoir host, highlighting the need to consider these ecological impacts when implementing fire management strategies.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results inform the ecological management of wildfire-prone areas and emphasize the importance of monitoring SNV prevalence in reservoir hosts following post-fire interventions.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's results are based on a single ENSO cycle and may not be generalizable to other regions or time periods. The evidence is moderate due to the observational nature of the study and potential confounding factors.

papers.title_zh: 烧毁老鼠:野火和火后重新播种对其 储存宿主 宿主 中的 Sin Nombre 病毒 患病率 的影响
papers.source_body_en: Worldwide, physical habitats and biological communities are being reshaped by wildfire. Such changes have obvious potential to alter pathogen ecology, yet few studies, outside of those focused on ectoparasites, have tested the effects of wildfire on pathogen prevalence in wildlife. Even fewer have focused on the impacts of strategies for post-fire remediation on pathogen circulation. Here, we investigated the effect of wildfire and wildfire mitigation on the prevalence and viral load of Sin Nombre virus (SNV) infection in its reservoir host, the western deer mouse, using a study design of matched burned, unburned, and post-burn reseeded sites in northern New Mexico. In total, we screened 411 individual deer mice for SNV via RT-qPCR and analyzed the effect of wildfire and wildfire mitigation on relative mouse abundance, individual infection probability, site-level prevalence and viral load. Relative abundance was highest at reseeded sites, and model selection indicated that habitat structure, particularly the gradient from closed canopy to open-herbaceous habitat, was consistently associated with increased relative abundance. Similarly, SNV prevalence was significantly higher in reseeded sites than either burned or unburned sites but did not differ in burned versus unburned sites. Viral load did not differ between burn history types, and zero-inflated gamma hurdle models did not identify any strong predictors of viral load. Serendipitously, we were also able to investigate the impacts of an El Nino Southern Oscillation (ENSO) cycle on patterns of infection in a subsample of sites that were studied during and one year after an ENSO year and found that SNV prevalence increased significantly post-ENSO. Both reseeding and ENSO deliver resource pulses that can support increases in mouse density and thereby enhance SNV transmission. The impacts of post-fire management practices on SNV prevalence in its reservoir host that were revealed in this study should be considered when implementing such strategies and when utilizing treated areas.
papers.abstract_zh: 在世界范围内,野火正在重塑自然栖息地和生物群落。这些变化显然有可能改变病原体生态,但除了针对体外寄生虫的研究外,很少有研究测试野火对野生动物中病原体 患病率 的影响。很少有人关注火灾后补救策略对病原体循环的影响。在这里,我们使用新墨西哥州北部匹配的烧毁、未烧毁和烧伤后重新播种地点的研究设计,研究了野火和野火缓解措施对 患病率 及其 储存宿主 宿主(西部鹿鼠)中 Sin Nombre 病毒 (SNV) 感染的病毒载量的影响。总共,我们通过 RT-qPCR 对 411 只鹿小鼠进行了 SNV 筛查,并分析了野火和野火缓解对相对小鼠丰度、个体感染概率、位点水平 患病率 和病毒载量的影响。重新播种地点的相对丰度最高,模型选择表明栖息地结构,特别是从封闭的树冠到开放草本栖息地的梯度,始终与相对丰度的增加相关。同样,重新播种地点的 SNV 患病率 显着高于烧毁或未烧毁地点,但烧毁与未烧毁地点没有差异。烧伤史类型之间的病毒载量没有差异,零膨胀伽玛障碍模型没有识别出任何强有力的病毒载量预测因子。偶然的是,我们还能够调查厄尔尼诺南方涛动 (ENSO) 周期对 ENSO 年期间和一年后研究的站点子样本感染模式的影响,并发现 SNV 患病率 在 ENSO 之后显着增加。重新播种和 ENSO 都提供资源脉冲,可以支持小鼠密度的增加,从而增强 SNV 传播。在实施此类策略和利用处理区域时,应考虑本研究中揭示的火后管理实践对其 储存宿主 宿主 中的 SNV 患病率 的影响。

papers.title: Emerging infectious diseases (Mpox, Nipah, and Andes): A narrative review of transmission, environmental survival, and disinfection
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Mpox, Nipah virus, and Andes virus are emerging infectious diseases that cause outbreaks associated with nosocomial transmission. METHODS: This narrative review summarizes the Mpox, Nipah virus, and Andes virus epidemiology, clinical manifestations, diagnosis, and treatment with a focus on environmental survival, susceptibility to antiseptics and disinfectants, and infection prevention. RESULTS: Mpox, Nipah virus, and Andes virus all survive in the environment and are capable of indirect transmission. All these viruses are enveloped and susceptible to commonly used antiseptics and surface disinfectants. CONCLUSIONS: Rapid identification of patients with known or suspected infections of these emerging viruses coupled with adherence to infection prevention recommendations will prevent healthcare-associated transmission.

analysis.summary_en: This narrative review examines three emerging infectious diseases—Mpox, Nipah virus, and Andes virus—with focus on epidemiology, clinical manifestations, diagnosis, treatment, environmental survival, and infection prevention. Andes virus is a target orthohantavirus associated with hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome. The review finds that all three viruses survive in the environment and are capable of indirect transmission, which contributes to nosocomial outbreak risk. As enveloped viruses, they are susceptible to commonly used antiseptics and surface disinfectants. The authors recommend rapid identification of patients with suspected infections coupled with adherence to infection prevention recommendations to prevent healthcare-associated transmission. Key evidence gaps include the lack of Andes virus-specific data reported separately from Mpox and Nipah findings, absence of reported review methodology details, and unspecified disinfection efficacy data for Andes virus specifically. Future research should validate environmental survival parameters and disinfectant susceptibility specific to Andes virus.

papers.title: Roles of Laboratory Animal Models in Zoonotic Diseases: A Review on Pathogenesis, Transmission, and Prevention Strategies
papers.abstract: Emerging zoonotic diseases have become an increasing concern for global health due to the rising incidence of pathogen transmission from animals to humans. The present study aimed to comprehensively synthesize the current knowledge on zoonotic disease outbreaks and transmission, with a specific focus on evaluating the role, applications, advantages, and limitations of laboratory animal models in this field. A peer-reviewed literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar for studies published between 2000 and 2026, supplemented by earlier pivotal studies. The current study evaluated a range of models, including conventional, humanized, and transgenic mice, hamsters, ferrets, guinea pigs, rabbits, non-human primates, and emerging alternatives, focusing on their utility, strengths, and drawbacks for studying host-pathogen interactions, immune responses, tissue tropism, and disease progression. The present study underscored the importance of animal models in the preclinical assessment of antiviral agents, vaccines, monoclonal antibodies, and innovative therapeutic strategies. Recent outbreaks caused by pathogens such as SARS-CoV-2, Nipah virus, H5N1 influenza virus, Mpox virus, Ebola virus, Marburg virus, hantavirus, and Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus have highlighted the urgent necessity to enhance comprehension of zoonotic disease emergence and transmission. The current challenges included species-specific differences, translational limitations, reproducibility, and ethical considerations, as well as emerging alternatives such as organoids, organ-on-chip platforms, and computational modeling, all of which were addressed in the present findings. Integrating advanced animal models with One Health approaches can strengthen disease surveillance and accelerate therapeutic development.

analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review synthesized peer-reviewed literature from PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar for studies published between 2000 and 2026, supplemented by earlier pivotal studies, to evaluate conventional, humanized, and transgenic mice, hamsters, ferrets, guinea pigs, rabbits, non-human primates, and emerging alternatives as animal models for zoonotic disease research.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that laboratory animal models are essential for preclinical assessment of antiviral agents, vaccines, monoclonal antibodies, and innovative therapeutic strategies, particularly in the context of recent outbreaks caused by pathogens such as hantaviruses, which have highlighted the urgent need to enhance understanding of zoonotic disease emergence and transmission.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies species-specific differences, translational limitations, reproducibility challenges, and ethical considerations as key limitations of current animal models, while also noting emerging alternatives such as organoids, organ-on-chip platforms, and computational modeling that address some of these gaps.

Key limitations include species-specific differences, translational challenges, and ethical concerns, though emerging alternatives like organoids and organ-on-chip platforms offer potential solutions. The review underscores the importance of integrating advanced models with One Health strategies to improve surveillance and accelerate therapeutic development for hantaviruses and other zoonotic diseases.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述探讨与人类疾病相关的哺乳动物正汉坦病毒,具体涉及肾综合征出血热(HFRS)及汉坦病毒肺综合征(HPS)或心肺综合征,重点关注实验室动物模型在理解宿主-病原体相互作用、免疫应答、组织嗜性及疾病进展中的作用。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述综合了 PubMed、Scopus、Web of Science 和 Google Scholar 2000 年至 2026 年间发表的研究的同行评审文献,并辅以早期的关键研究,以评估传统、人源化和转基因小鼠、仓鼠、雪貂、豚鼠、兔子、非人类灵长类动物以及作为人畜共患疾病研究动物模型的新兴替代品。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述得出的结论是,实验动物模型对于 抗病毒药物 药物、疫苗、单克隆抗体和创新治疗策略的临床前评估至关重要,特别是在最近由汉坦病毒等病原体引起的 暴发 的背景下,这凸显了迫切需要加强对人畜共患病的出现和 传播 的了解。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述将物种特异性差异、翻译限制、再现性挑战和伦理考虑确定为当前动物模型的主要局限性,同时还指出了新兴的替代方案,例如类器官、芯片器官平台和计算模型,以解决其中一些差距。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该综述强调需要将先进的动物模型与 One Health 方法相结合,以加强疾病 监测 并加速治疗开发,特别是针对汉坦病毒和其他人畜共患病原体。

papers.title: Non-State Actors and The Due Diligence Obligation to Protect Healthcare Facilities in Cyberspace: Is the World Prepared for The Next Pandemic?
papers.abstract: This article presents a novel approach by developing a lex specialis due diligence framework based on the elements identified in the ICJ Advisory Opinion on Climate Change, which by analogy, establishes sector-specific elements to protect healthcare facilities from cyberattacks by Non-State Actors (NSAs). Cyberattacks by NSAs during the COVID-19 pandemic exposed the risks, including the disruption of essential healthcare services and hindrance of positive obligations to ensure the rights to health, life, and privacy, among others. Existing instruments, including the Budapest Convention, the Tallinn Manuals, and the Oxford Statements, offer an important but incomplete framework. Meanwhile, the recent UN Convention Against Cybercrime (not yet in force) represents another missed opportunity to clarify due diligence obligations regarding the actions of NSAs targeting critical infrastructure, such as healthcare facilities. Therefore, this research highlights the inadequacy of simply extending general international law to cyberspace and argues in favor of establishing a sector-specific due diligence framework to protect healthcare facilities from cyberattacks by NSAs. Recent Ebola and hantavirus cases reinforce this conclusion.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study addresses the need for a specialized legal framework to protect healthcare facilities from cyberattacks by Non-State Actors (NSAs), particularly in the context of pandemics. It highlights the risks posed by such attacks, including disruption of essential healthcare services and violation of human rights.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a legal and policy analysis examining the adequacy of existing international instruments in addressing cyber threats to healthcare facilities. It focuses on the implications of these threats during the COVID-19 pandemic and considers the broader context of public health and human rights.
analysis.methods: The methods involve a review of international legal frameworks, including the Budapest Convention, the Tallinn Manuals, and the Oxford Statements, to assess their applicability to cyber threats in healthcare. The study also evaluates the UN Convention Against Cybercrime and its potential to address these issues.
analysis.main_results: The study concludes that existing legal instruments are insufficient to address the specific risks posed by cyberattacks on healthcare facilities by NSAs. It identifies gaps in the current frameworks and emphasizes the need for a sector-specific due diligence approach.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as evidence of the inadequacy of general international law in cyberspace, arguing for the development of a specialized legal framework to protect healthcare facilities. This approach is novel in its application of the lex specialis principle to cybersecurity in public health.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the need for targeted legal and policy measures to safeguard healthcare infrastructure from cyber threats, which is critical for maintaining public health security and upholding human rights during pandemics.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on existing legal texts and lacks empirical data on the frequency or impact of cyberattacks on healthcare facilities. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on legal analysis rather than direct observation or experimentation.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 这项研究解决了对专门法律框架的需求,以保护医疗机构免受非国家行为者 (NSA) 的网络攻击,特别是在流行病背景下。它强调了此类攻击带来的风险,包括基本医疗服务中断和侵犯人权。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是一项法律和政策分析,旨在检验现有国际文书在应对医疗机构网络威胁方面的充分性。它重点关注 COVID-19 大流行期间这些威胁的影响,并考虑更广泛的公共卫生和人权背景。
elements_zh.methods: 这些方法涉及对国际法律框架的审查,包括《布达佩斯公约》、《塔林手册》和《牛津声明》,以评估其对医疗保健网络威胁的适用性。该研究还评估了《联合国打击网络犯罪公约》及其解决这些问题的潜力。
elements_zh.main_results: 该研究的结论是,现有的法律文书不足以解决国家安全局对医疗机构进行网络攻击所带来的具体风险。它确定了当前框架中的差距,并强调需要采取针对特定部门的尽职调查方法。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为网络空间一般国际法不足的证据,主张制定专门的法律框架来保护医疗保健设施。这种方法的新颖之处在于将特别法原则应用于公共卫生网络安全。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,需要采取有针对性的法律和政策措施来保护医疗基础设施免受网络威胁,这对于在大流行期间维护公共卫生安全和维护人权至关重要。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其对现有法律文本的依赖而受到限制,并且缺乏有关网络攻击对医疗机构的频率或影响的经验数据。证据是中等的,因为它是基于法律分析而不是直接观察或实验。

papers.abstract_zh: 本文提出了一种新颖的方法,即根据国际法院气候变化咨询意见中确定的要素制定特别法尽职调查框架,以此类推,建立特定部门的要素,以保护医疗机构免受非国家行为者 (NSA) 的网络攻击。COVID-19 大流行期间国家安全局的网络攻击暴露了风险,包括基本医疗保健服务的中断以及确保健康权、生命权和隐私权等积极义务的阻碍。现有文书,包括《布达佩斯公约》、《塔林手册》和《牛津声明》,提供了一个重要但不完整的框架。与此同时,最近的《联合国打击网络犯罪公约》(尚未生效)再次错失了澄清针对国家安全机构针对医疗设施等关键基础设施的行为的尽职调查义务的机会。因此,本研究强调了简单地将一般国际法扩展到网络空间的不足,并主张建立针对特定部门的尽职调查框架,以保护医疗机构免受国家安全局的网络攻击。最近的埃博拉和汉坦病毒病例强化了这一结论。
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出了一种新颖的方法,即根据国际法院气候变化咨询意见中确定的要素制定特别法尽职调查框架,以此类推,建立特定部门的要素,以保护医疗机构免受非国家行为者 (NSA) 的网络攻击。COVID-19 大流行期间国家安全局的网络攻击暴露了风险,包括基本医疗保健服务的中断以及确保健康权、生命权和隐私权等积极义务的阻碍。现有文书,包括《布达佩斯公约》、《塔林手册》和《牛津声明》,提供了一个重要但不完整的框架。与此同时,最近的《联合国打击网络犯罪公约》(尚未生效)再次错失了澄清针对国家安全机构针对医疗设施等关键基础设施的行为的尽职调查义务的机会。因此,本研究强调了简单地将一般国际法扩展到网络空间的不足,并主张建立针对特定部门的尽职调查框架,以保护医疗机构免受国家安全局的网络攻击。最近的埃博拉和汉坦病毒病例强化了这一结论。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 这项研究解决了对专门法律框架的需求,以保护医疗机构免受非国家行为者 (NSA) 的网络攻击,特别是在流行病背景下。它强调了此类攻击带来的风险,包括基本医疗服务中断和侵犯人权。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是一项法律和政策分析,旨在检验现有国际文书在应对医疗机构网络威胁方面的充分性。它重点关注 COVID-19 大流行期间这些威胁的影响,并考虑更广泛的公共卫生和人权背景。
analysis_zh.methods: 这些方法涉及对国际法律框架的审查,包括《布达佩斯公约》、《塔林手册》和《牛津声明》,以评估其对医疗保健网络威胁的适用性。该研究还评估了《联合国打击网络犯罪公约》及其解决这些问题的潜力。
analysis_zh.main_results: 该研究的结论是,现有的法律文书不足以解决国家安全局对医疗机构进行网络攻击所带来的具体风险。它确定了当前框架中的差距,并强调需要采取针对特定部门的尽职调查方法。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为网络空间一般国际法不足的证据,主张制定专门的法律框架来保护医疗保健设施。这种方法的新颖之处在于将特别法原则应用于公共卫生网络安全。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,需要采取有针对性的法律和政策措施来保护医疗基础设施免受网络威胁,这对于在大流行期间维护公共卫生安全和维护人权至关重要。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其对现有法律文本的依赖而受到限制,并且缺乏有关网络攻击对医疗机构的频率或影响的经验数据。证据是中等的,因为它是基于法律分析而不是直接观察或实验。
